what_its_for: Amikacin is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections, including infections of the lungs, urinary tract, blood, skin, bones, and joints. It works by stopping the growth and killing harmful bacteria in your body. It is also used in inhaled form (Arikayce) to treat a specific lung infection called Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) in adults who have not responded to other treatments.
how_to_take: Amikacin is given as a shot (injection) into a muscle or vein (IV) by a healthcare provider in a hospital or clinic setting. You will NOT give this medicine to yourself at home in most cases. The inhaled form (Arikayce) is breathed in using a special nebulizer device. If you are using the inhaled form at home, carefully follow the instructions your doctor or pharmacist gave you for using the nebulizer. Always use it at the same time each day and never swallow the liquid — it is only for breathing in.
dosing: Your dose will be decided by your doctor based on your weight, the type of infection you have, and how well your kidneys are working. Doses are usually given once daily or in divided doses every 8 to 12 hours. The inhaled form (Arikayce) is typically used once daily. Never change your dose on your own. Your doctor will do regular blood tests to make sure the amount of medicine in your body is safe and effective.
missed_dose: Since this medicine is usually given by a healthcare provider, a missed dose is unlikely in a hospital setting. If you are using the inhaled form at home and you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. Call your doctor or pharmacist if you are unsure what to do.
storage: Store the inhaled liquid form (Arikayce) in the refrigerator at 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8°C). You may also store it at room temperature (up to 77°F or 25°C) for up to 4 weeks. Do not freeze. Keep it away from light and out of the reach of children. Do not use the medicine if it looks cloudy, has changed color, or has particles floating in it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid other medications that can harm your kidneys or ears unless your doctor approves them. These include other antibiotics like gentamicin or tobramycin, water pills (diuretics) like furosemide, and certain pain relievers like ibuprofen or naproxen used regularly. Tell your doctor about ALL medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take. Avoid becoming dehydrated — drink plenty of fluids unless your doctor tells you otherwise. Do not use the inhaled nebulizer solution if it has been stored improperly or looks unusual.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: hearing loss, ringing or buzzing in your ears, dizziness or spinning sensation (vertigo), loss of balance, decreased urination or dark-colored urine (signs of kidney problems), numbness or tingling in your hands or feet, muscle twitching or weakness, difficulty breathing or wheezing after inhaling the medicine, rash, itching, or swelling of the face or throat, or severe diarrhea that is watery or bloody. These could be signs of serious side effects that need immediate attention.
when_it_works: You may start to feel better within a few days of starting treatment, but it is very important to complete the full course of treatment your doctor has prescribed. Do NOT stop taking this medicine early even if you feel better, as the infection may not be fully treated and could come back stronger. For the inhaled form used for MAC lung infection, improvement may take several months of treatment.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over): Your kidneys may not work as well, which means the medicine can build up in your body and cause harm. Your doctor will monitor you very closely and may adjust your dose. Kidney disease: If you have kidney problems, your dose will need to be lowered and you will need frequent blood tests. Pregnancy: Amikacin may harm an unborn baby, including causing hearing loss. Tell your doctor immediately if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Breastfeeding: Small amounts of amikacin may pass into breast milk. Talk to your doctor about the risks and benefits before breastfeeding. Children: Amikacin can be used in children, including newborns, but doses are carefully calculated by the doctor based on the child's weight and age.
